    "issue_type": "Insecure Randomness for Session ID",
    "severity": "high",
    "file": "t18.js",
    "line": 4,
    "evidence": "const sessionId = Math.random().toString(36).slice(2) + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2);",
    "llm_reasoning": "Math.random() is a PRNG that is not cryptographically secure. It is predictable, meaning an attacker could potentially guess valid session IDs if they can observe enough samples or determine the internal state of the generator. This leads to session hijacking vulnerabilities.",
    "suggested_fix": "Use the built-in crypto module: const crypto = require('crypto'); const sessionId = crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex');",
    "confidence": 1.0,

  {
    "issue_type": "Session Fixation / Lack of Session Expiration",
    "severity": "medium",
    "file": "t18.js",
    "line": 6,
    "evidence": "sessions.set(sessionId, { userId, createdAt: Date.now() });",
    "llm_reasoning": "The session management implementation stores sessions in an in-memory Map without any mechanism for expiration or cleanup. Over time, this will lead to a memory leak (Denial of Service) and increases the window of opportunity for an attacker to use a stolen session token, as sessions never expire.",
    "suggested_fix": "Implement a TTL (Time-To-Live) mechanism for sessions and periodically prune expired entries from the Map, or use a dedicated session store like Redis with built-in expiration.",

  }
